## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## inst/scripts/make-data.R
##
## The documentation below is based on controlled-access
## primary data (EGA, dbGaP) and on intermediate files that are too large to
## distribute with the package, so the script is NOT intended to be run
## end-to-end. It records what was done, from what
## source, with what tool, at what parameters, so that the files in
## inst/extdata/ can be traced back to their origin and regenerated by users
## with appropriate access.
##
## All example files cover a demonstration region on chromosome 1
## (chr1:43,000,000-50,000,000, hg38) in 10 mCRPC samples from 
## Zhao et al, Nature Genetics, 2025.

## 1. Hi-C contact matrices: inst/extdata/example_hic/sample*.hic
##
## Source
## ------
## Paired-end Hi-C FASTQs for mCRPC samples were
## obtained from the European Genome-phenome Archive (EGA) under the
## following controlled-access datasets:
##   EGAD00001009408
##   EGAD00001009417
## License: EGA controlled access; a Data Access Agreement is required
## to obtain the raw FASTQs.
## Then 10 samples were randomly selected to make the example dataset.
##
## Preprocessing
## -------------
## FASTQs were processed to per-sample .hic files following 4DN pipeline.
## Briefly, we first aligned the raw sequencing reads (i.e., fastq files) 
## with BWA MEM (v0.7.17), and the aligned reads were paired, sorted, and 
## filtered with Pairtools (v0.3.0) and converted into pairs files. Next, 
## we normalized paired data to generate matrix files with Juicertools57 
## for Juicer (v1.5) (hic files).
##
## Subsetting for the package (demo region extraction)
## ---------------------------------------------------
## Each full-size .hic was reduced to a small .hic restricted to
## chr1:43,000,000-50,000,000 at the resolutions used by loopQTL. The
## reduction extracts contact records touching the demo region from the
## .hic via strawr::straw(), rebuilds a minimal pairs file from those
## records, and runs Juicer Tools pre on the minimal pairs file to produce
## a valid .hic with the same normalization method.
##
## Sketch (per sample):
##
##   library(strawr)
##   res <- 10000                         # analysis resolution (bp)
##   region <- "1:43000000:50000000"      # Juicer-style region string
##
##   pairs <- strawr::straw(
##       norm       = "NONE",
##       fname      = "full/sample1.hic",
##       chr1loc    = region,
##       chr2loc    = region,
##       unit       = "BP",
##       binsize    = res,
##       matrix     = "observed"
##   )
##
##   ## Write a minimal pairs file and rebuild a .hic
##   ## (see Juicer Tools pre --help for the expected columns)
##   writePairsTxt(pairs, "tmp.pairs")
##   system2("java", c("-jar", "juicer_tools.jar", "pre",
##                     "tmp.pairs", "inst/extdata/example_hic/sample1.hic",
##                     "hg38"))


## =============================================================================
## 2. Loop calls: inst/extdata/example_loops/sample*_loops.bedpe
## =============================================================================
##
## Source and method
## -----------------
## Per-sample significant chromatin loops were called from the full-size .hic
## files using FitHiC. Only long range loops (anchor distance > 30KB) with significance
## (q-value <= 0.2) were kept for the loopQTL analysis demo. 
##
## Subsetting
## ----------
## Each sample's full-size BEDPE of significant loops was filtered to loops
## with both anchors overlapping the demo region:
##
##   library(GenomicRanges)
##   library(InteractionSet)
##
##   full <- read.table("full/sample1_loops.bedpe", sep = "\t", header = FALSE)
##   colnames(full)[1:6] <- c("chrA","startA","endA","chrB","startB","endB")
##
##   region <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(43000000, 50000000))
##   anchA  <- GRanges(full$chrA, IRanges(full$startA, full$endA))
##   anchB  <- GRanges(full$chrB, IRanges(full$startB, full$endB))
##   keep   <- overlapsAny(anchA, region) & overlapsAny(anchB, region)
##
##   write.table(full[keep, ], "inst/extdata/example_loops/sample1_loops.bedpe",
##               sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)


## =============================================================================
## 3. Genotypes: inst/extdata/example.vcf.gz (+ .tbi)
## =============================================================================
##
## Source
## ------
## Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) reads matched to the Hi-C mCRPC samples
## were obtained from dbGaP accession:
##   phs001648
## License: dbGaP controlled access.
##
## Preprocessing (full pipeline)
## -----------------------------
## Standard GATK germline short-variant pipeline:
##   1. Alignment to GRCh38 (BWA-MEM).
##   2. Mark duplicates (Picard MarkDuplicates).
##   3. BQSR (GATK BaseRecalibrator / ApplyBQSR).
##   4. Joint calling across samples (GATK HaplotypeCaller + GenotypeGVCFs).
##   5. VQSR / hard-filter PASS variants.
## The VCF header carried through from the full callset is still visible
## in the shipped example file (GATK FORMAT/INFO fields).
##
## Subsetting
## ----------
## The full chr1 VCF was restricted to a tight core region, bgzip-compressed,
## and tabix-indexed:
##
##   bcftools view full/samples.vcf.gz \
##       --regions chr1:45600000-46150000 \
##     | bgzip > inst/extdata/example.vcf.gz
##   tabix -p vcf inst/extdata/example.vcf.gz


## =============================================================================
## 4. Gene annotation: inst/extdata/example.gtf.gz
## =============================================================================
##
## Source
## ------
## GENCODE Human basic annotation, release 29 (hg38).
##   https://www.gencodegenes.org/human/release_29.html
## File: gencode.v29.basic.annotation.gtf.gz
##
## Subsetting
## ----------
## Filtered to records on chr1 whose feature interval overlaps the demo
## region, keeping the original GENCODE two-line header:
##
##   zcat gencode.v29.basic.annotation.gtf.gz \
##     | awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"}
##            /^#/ {print; next}
##            $1=="chr1" && $4<=50000000 && $5>=43000000' \
##     | gzip > inst/extdata/example.gtf.gz


## =============================================================================
## 5. Regulatory peaks: inst/extdata/example_annotation.bed
## =============================================================================
##
## Source
## ------
## Consensus H3K27ac ChIP-seq peak set generated from mCRPC samples
## deposited in GEO (GSE130408).
##
## Processing
## ----------
## Per-sample narrowPeak calls (MACS2) were merged across mCRPC samples to
## form a consensus set (retain peaks present in >= 2 samples) The resulting
## BED3 was kept genome-wide; it is NOT subset to the demo region, so that 
## downstream annotation examples in the vignette can demonstrate overlap 
## behavior at the whole-chromosome level.


## =============================================================================
## 6. Samplesheet: inst/extdata/example_samplesheet.tsv
## =============================================================================
##
## A TSV file with matched ID to its per-sample .hic file,
## per-sample loops BEDPE, and total cis-contact count ("cis" column,
## pre-computed from the full .hic before subsetting). Format is documented
## in ?loopQTLsetup().
